newsitem.title: UK: UK shares recover as rate hopes lift Europe.
newsitem.headline: UK shares recover as rate hopes lift Europe.

text.p: Rising continental markets and strong gilts dragged UK shares off their lows late in the session on Thursday, after a day dogged by weakness in drug stocks and lacking the usual Wall Street stimulus.

The FTSE 100 index closed up 1.0 point at 4,050.2, with gainers nearly matching decliners 45 to 48. The index was stuck in a narrow range for much of the session, as New York took its annual Thanksgiving break.
Traders said the market was likely to be marooned near its current levels with Wall Street unlikely to see much action in tomorrow's post-holiday session.

Yet a rise in Germany's Dax to a record close gave London a late boost, after comments from a Bank of France official in favour of a stronger dollar were taken as a hint that European rates might move lower.
In the UK there were also hopes for a year-end rally, helping counter the market's torpor following Tuesday's dull-but-worthy budget.

"Pundits seem to think there's still some upside momentum left in the UK market, with perhaps another 150 points by year- end," said Mike Wolfgang, head of UK equities at Barclays Global Investors. "Maybe that would count as a year end rally."
"We are not in any rush to put money in," Wolfgang said, "but that doesn't mean we are particularly bearish."

Drug stocks were again the main focus of interest with Glaxo Wellcome down 21p at 987-1/2 after a Merrill Lynch downgrade and Zeneca Group down 15-1/2p at 16.52 stg as speculative interest cooled on the perennial bid favourite.

Yet SmithKline Beecham rallied sharply in late trading for a second day amid switching in the sector and talk of a bid or merger with Switzerland's Roche Holding. SmithKline closed 22p higher at a record 830-1/2p.
Elsewhere electricals retailer Dixons Group was among the day's biggest gainers, recovering 24-1/2 at 572 after the budget blow of tax on its profitable extended warranties.

Royal Bank of Scotland was another gainer, up 7-1/2p at 529-1/2 after annual results at the top of analysts expectations, and transport group Stagecoach leapt 48p to a record 631-1/2 after also beating analyst forecasts.

Yet BOC Group Plc fell 11-1/2p to 888-1/2 on profit-taking after yesterday reaching a four-month high and P&O fell 12-1/2p to 583-1/2 after its proposed ferry merger with Sweden's Stena was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission.

Overall trading volume reached a modest 618.7 million shares by 1708 GMT, boosted by 22 million in Mercury World Mining investment trust and 15 million Asda Group, up 2p at 118-1/2 after industry data showed it gaining market share.

Figures from AGB showed Asda increasing market share to 13.4 percent in November from 13.2 percent a month before. Rival supermarket operator Safeway, also said to be winning in the fiercely competitive supermarket sector, was up 7p at 387.
Second-line stocks were also mixed, with the FTSE 250 up 4.7 points at 4,416.7. The Reuters-HSBC 150 index of leading British stocks was up 0.35 points at 1,094.96.
Strong gilts helped support the UK equity market, with the December long gilt up 13/32 at 111.
German government Bunds also rose strongly on revived rate hopes the Dax stock index rose some 20 points to a record high.
Yet for much of the session it was the Dow's slight fall on Wednesday, and Wall Street's closure for Thanksgiving, that cast a shadow over shares.
"New York was down yesterday and invariably there won't be many people around tomorrow," said one senior sales trader. "That will probably leave us to drift but without any real selling pressure."

After reaching a record high in early trading on Tuesday, the UK market also continued to suffer from fears that the budget had not done enough to clamp down on inflation and prevent a need for further rises in UK interest rates.
Imperial Tobacco rose 13p to 382-1/2p as old rumours of a dawn raid resurfaced but MAM fell 17-1/2p to 12.25 stg as Kleinwort advised "take profits."

BSkyB fell 4-1/2p to 517-1/2p after a negative report in the Wall Street Journal Europe and comments from the industry watchdog that he would prevent the first market entrant into digital television from exploiting a monopoly position.
-- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4027
